newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain holds three suspected ETA youth supporters.
newsitem.headline: Spain holds three suspected ETA youth supporters.

text.p: Spanish police said they arrested three people on Wednesday suspected of belonging to a violent youth group that supports Basque separatist guerrillas.
The three were arrested after they tried to attack an employment office in the old quarter of the Basque regional capital Vitoria, state radio said.
Police said they were investigating the relationship between the detainees and the separatist group ETA, which has killed some 800 people in a nearly 30-year campaign for an independent Basque state.
Spain's government has promised to crack down on the violent youths who support ETA after the guerrillas killed a young politician earlier this month and set off a massive public outcry.
Days after ETA killed 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, the government announced plans to criminalise acts of vandalism. Officials say the groups have created a climate of fear in the troubled region.
The youths mask their faces and go on weekly rampages through Basque cities and towns, firebombing banks, buses and public property in the name of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Police have arrested about 100 of the young hoodlums since February, when efforts to stop street violence began in earnest.
